The discussion of the Qur'anic words: "Said," [i.e., Nuh] after he had exerted his utmost effort and his means were exhausted, over those long periods: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people night and day﴾ [71:5], meaning to monotheism (tawhid, affirming God's oneness) and righteous action, ﴿constantly, without slackening or laxity﴾ [71:5].

﴿But my calling only increased them in flight﴾ [71:6], meaning: away from the truth You sent me with.

﴿And whenever I call them, that You may forgive them﴾ [71:7], meaning: to faith, ﴿that You may forgive them through it﴾ [71:7]. ﴿They put their fingers in their ears﴾ [71:7], meaning: they stopped their hearing from listening to the call. ﴿And covered themselves with their garments﴾ [71:7], meaning: they wrapped themselves in them out of aversion to looking at the face of the one who advises them in religion. ﴿And persisted﴾ [71:7], meaning: in evil and disbelief. ﴿And grew arrogant with great arrogance﴾ [71:7], meaning: they considered themselves too great to submit to the truth and to accept the advice I called them to.

﴿Then I called them openly﴾ [71:8]. ﴿Then I proclaimed to them and spoke to them privately in secret﴾ [71:9]. Meaning: I called them time after time, in various ways, ranging from open and manifest calling without concealment, to proclaiming and shouting at them, and to speaking to them privately between myself and them in secrecy. These stages are the utmost that one who enjoins good (al-amr bil-ma'ruf, commanding what is right) and forbids wrong (al-nahy 'an al-munkar, prohibiting what is wrong) can do.

﴿So I said: Seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾ [71:10], meaning: ask Him for pardon for what has passed, through sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh, repentance that is genuine and unreserved). ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving﴾ [71:10], meaning: to the sins of those who repent and turn back.

﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾ [71:11], meaning: the rain, ﴿in succession﴾ [71:11], meaning: continuous.

﴿And provide you with wealth and children﴾ [71:12], meaning: He will increase them for you. ﴿And make for you gardens and make for you rivers﴾ [71:12], meaning: to irrigate your gardens and farms.

﴿What is wrong with you that you do not expect dignity from God﴾ [71:13], meaning: you do not see any greatness in Him, since you associate with Him what neither hears nor sees. The negation of hope is intended to mean the negation of its necessary consequence, which is belief, for emphasis. It has also been permitted that "hope" here means "fear," i.e., what is wrong with you that you do not fear God's greatness. From this is the poet's saying:

When the bee has stung him, he does not hope for its sting.

Al-Shihab (al-Alusi) said: this is the more apparent meaning.

﴿And He has created you in stages﴾ [71:14], meaning: in successive states: first dust, then a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a chewed lump, then a fetus, and thus stage after stage. That is, the knowledge of this entails intense awe of His punishment and seizure, given the greatness of His power. This is about yourselves. In this way, His overwhelming greatness and dominating power are inferred from His cosmic signs, as He said:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[21–25] ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in nothing but loss.﴾ ﴿And they have plotted a great plot.﴾ [Nuh: 22] (p-5937) ﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth or Ya'uq or Nasr."﴾ [Nuh: 23] ﴿And they have misled many, so increase the wrongdoers in nothing but error.﴾ [Nuh: 24] ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter the Fire, and they found for themselves, besides Allah, no helpers.﴾ [Nuh: 25]

﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me﴾: that is, they opposed my command and rejected what I called them to of guidance and right conduct. ﴿And they followed one whose wealth and children increase him in nothing but loss﴾: that is, their leaders who were followed, the people of wealth and status, who turned away from the truth, those whom their wealth and children deceived, so they perished through them and lost the happiness of both abodes.

﴿And they have plotted a great plot﴾ [Nuh: 22]: that is, one whose greatness was extreme, for the kubbar (intensified form) is greater than the kabir (great).

﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth or Ya'uq or Nasr."﴾ [Nuh: 23] Qatadah said: these were gods that the people of Noah worshipped, and then the Arabs worshipped them after that.

He said: Wadd belonged to the Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal; Suwa' belonged to Hudhayl; Yaghuth belonged to the Banu Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jarf; Ya'uq belonged to Hamdan; and Nasr belonged to Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar.

In another report he said: "By Allah, each of them was nothing but a piece of wood, or a clay figure, or a stone."

Ibn Jarir said: their account, as it has reached us, is from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: they were righteous men from the children of Adam, and they had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: "If we were to make images of them, it would be more eager for us toward worship when we remember them." So they made images of them. When they died and others came after them, Iblis whispered to them, saying: "They were only worshipping them, and by them rain is given to them," so they worshipped them.

(p-5938) Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The idols that were among the people of Noah passed to the Arabs afterward. As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal; as for Suwa', it belonged to Hudhayl; as for Yaghuth, it belonged to Murad, then to the Banu Ghutayf at al-Jarf near Saba'; as for Ya'uq, it belonged to Hamdan; and as for Nasr, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhu al-Kala'. They were names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they died, Satan inspired their people to set up at their gathering places, where they used to sit, stone markers (ansab), and to name them after them. They did so, but they were not worshipped until those people died and knowledge was lost, and then they were worshipped.

Notes:

First: al-Razi said: there is a difficulty in their transmission from the people of Noah to the Arabs, because the world was destroyed in the time of the Flood, so how did those idols remain, and how did they pass to the Arabs? It cannot be said that Noah, peace be upon him, placed them in the Ark and preserved them, because he, peace be upon him, came to negate them and break them, so how could it be said that he placed them in the Ark seeking to preserve them? End of his words.

We say: its answer is self-evident, namely that their transmission to the Arabs occurred through the transmission of the conditions of the people of Noah and their descendants and their customs, through the tongues of travelers and storytellers, for the course of an earlier generation in a later age, and the custom of the successor is to record the predecessor. It is clear that the soul is more inclined to ignorance than to knowledge, especially when the reprehensible is made attractive to it in a form it inclines toward, so it becomes closer to it. Thus, after the vanishing of knowledge and its bearers, what happened happened of their worship, as the report of Ibn 'Abbas in al-Bukhari indicates: "until those people died and knowledge was lost, and then they were worshipped." It is strange that al-Razi does not find an exit from his question, while he is on the edge of a thyme (i.e., his point is weak/easily refuted).

Second: al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: al-Waqidi related that Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a bird. This is anomalous (shadhdh), and the well-known view is that they were in human form, which is what is implied by the previously mentioned reports about the cause of their worship. End of his words.

Third: Ibn al-Qayyim said in I'lam... (Ighathat al-Lahfan): The first thing by which Satan deceived the worshippers of idols was through devotion at graves and the images of their occupants, so that they would remember them through them, as Allah, glorified is He, related their stories in His Book, saying: ﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods..."﴾ [Nuh: 23], and so on...

Then he said: Satan's manipulation of the polytheists in worshipping idols has many causes; he manipulated each people according to the measure of their minds: one group he invited to worship them through venerating the dead whose images those idols were made in the likeness of, as has passed concerning the people of Noah, peace be upon him. For this reason, "the Prophet (ﷺ) cursed those who take mosques over graves and lamps," and "forbade prayer toward graves," and "asked his Lord, glorified is He, that his grave not become an idol worshipped," and "forbade his community to take his grave as a festival," and said: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who took the graves of their prophets as mosques," and "commanded the leveling of graves and the effacing of images." But the polytheists refused except to oppose him in all of that, either out of ignorance or out of obstinacy toward the people of monotheism, and it did not harm them at all... to the end of what he mentioned, may Allah have mercy on him.

Second: al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: al-Waqidi related that Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a bird. This is anomalous (shadhdh), and the well-known view is that they were in human form, which is what is implied by the previously mentioned reports about the cause of their worship. End of his words.

Third: Ibn al-Qayyim said in I'lam... (Ighathat al-Lahfan): The first thing by which Satan deceived the worshippers of idols was through devotion at graves and the images of their occupants, so that they would remember them through them, as Allah, glorified is He, related their stories in His Book, saying: ﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods..."﴾ [Nuh: 23], and so on...

Then he said: Satan's manipulation of the polytheists in worshipping idols has many causes; he manipulated each people according to the measure of their minds: one group he invited to worship them through venerating the dead whose images those idols were made in the likeness of, as has passed concerning the people of Noah, peace be upon him. For this reason, "the Prophet (ﷺ) cursed those who take mosques over graves and lamps," and "forbade prayer toward graves," and "asked his Lord, glorified is He, that his grave not become an idol worshipped," and "forbade his community to take his grave as a festival," and said: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who took the graves of their prophets as mosques," and "commanded the leveling of graves and the effacing of images." But the polytheists refused except to oppose him in all of that, either out of ignorance or out of obstinacy toward the people of monotheism, and it did not harm them at all... to the end of what he mentioned, may Allah have mercy on him.

(p-5939)

﴿And they have misled﴾ [Nuh: 24]: that is, the leaders ﴿many﴾ [Nuh: 24]: that is, a great multitude of creatures; or the idols, as in His words: ﴿My Lord, they have indeed led astray many of mankind﴾ [Ibrahim: 36]. ﴿So increase the wrongdoers in nothing but error﴾ [Nuh: 24]: that is, abandonment and gradual leading on. He made this supplication because he had despaired of their faith.

Abu al-Su'ud said: he placed the apparent noun in place of their pronoun, to record upon them excessive wrongdoing, and to give the reason for the curse upon them: ﴿Because of their sins﴾ [Nuh: 25]: that is, on account of them ﴿they were drowned﴾ [Nuh: 25]: that is, by the Flood ﴿and then made to enter the Fire﴾ [Nuh: 25]: that is, they were made to taste by it the punishment of the Fire ﴿and they found for themselves, besides Allah, no helpers﴾ [Nuh: 25].

Al-Zamakhshari said: it is an allusion to their taking gods besides Allah, and that they are incapable of helping them, and a mockery of them, as if he said: they found for themselves, besides Allah, no gods that would help them and protect them from the punishment of Allah, as in His words:

﴿Or do they have gods that protect them from Us?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 43]

And al-Razi said: since it has been established that He, exalted is He, is the One capable of all things that are capable, the claim of intermediaries is invalidated.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 71, verses 26–28:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26–28] ﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller.﴾ ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except a wicked, ungrateful one.﴾ [Nuh: 27] ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house in faith and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.﴾ [Nuh: 28]

﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller.﴾ Meaning: anyone.

Ibn Jarir said: By ad-Ayyar (dweller) is meant one who moves about the earth, going and coming within it. It is fa'al from ad-dawaran (revolving). The original was daywar; the yaa' and the waw came together, the yaa' preceded the waw while being sukun, and the waw was assimilated into it, and both became a doubled yaa'. The Arabs say: "There is no dayyar in it, nor 'arib, nor dawiyy, nor safir, nor nafikh dharama."

(p-5941) ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾ [Nuh: 27] from the path of truth.

﴿and will not beget except a wicked, ungrateful one.﴾ [Nuh: 27] Abu as-Su'ud said: Meaning: except one who will become wicked and disbelieving. He described them by what they would become. It seems to be an apology against what might be objected to him: that the supplication for total destruction, while it is possible that among their descendants there would be one who believes, is objectionable. He said it because of the firm knowledge of what would come from them and their descendants after he had tested them and surveyed their conditions for nearly a thousand years.

Some of them said: Noah, peace be upon him, grew weary of his people's call and became distressed, and anger overcame him, so he supplicated his Lord for the destruction and subjugation of his people. He judged by the apparent state that one veiled, over whom disbelief has prevailed, begets only its like, for the drop that arises from a wicked, veiled soul and is nurtured in its darkened forms accepts only a soul like itself, like the seed that grows only from its own kind and stock. End.

﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ [Nuh: 28] Ibn Jarir said: Meaning: My Lord, pardon me, and cover my sins and the sins of my parents. ﴿and whoever enters my house in faith﴾ [Nuh: 28] Ibn Jarir said: Meaning: whoever enters my mosque and place of prayer, praying, a believer in the obligation of Your duty upon him. It was also said: "my house" means my dwelling.

﴿and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.﴾ [Nuh: 28] Meaning: ruin and loss.
